description: Pair this MCP server to an open SurfCAD tab via the local WebSocket relay. Copy the 8-character code from SurfCAD → Local agent → Show pairing code, or run npx surfcad-mcp login --code with the join code. call register_webhook { url, bearer? } if you can receive https webhooks, otherwise poll read_messages. When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left. Call set_status { state: "building" } only once you have everything you need and are actually creating or editing geometry. Be interactive: post_progress while working, especially during long reasoning. A fresh process per tool call is normal and stays present. A long-lived process is optional, never required. Call close_session when done, never on exit. Required after every in-viewer prompt (full order: guide { topic: "chat" }): ack first with set_status { state: "responding", id: <prompt id> } before any other tool (bouncing dots), then one short reply_to_user { in_reply_to, final: false }. The tab holds that reply for 10 seconds, then folds the chat and shows the working spinner. Required after every pair: register_webhook again (process memory only). No webhook: loop read_messages { wait_ms: 10000 } while connected; polling is not activity. An empty immediate read does not mean the user never sent. After pairing call guide { topic: "start" } (How to build in SurfCAD: block out first, features first, hardware as patterned parts) before the first model call.

code.description: 8-character pairing code from the SurfCAD Local agent panel
